findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is abstract and cannot be instantiated
findings.body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now extends StatefulDetectorHandler but does not implement the required abstract methods: `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. The `Detector.detector_handler` property (detector.py line 86) calls `group_type.detector_handler(self)`, which attempts to instantiate this class. If any Detector is created with type `metric_alert_fire`, Python will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler with abstract methods ...` at runtime. The previous implementation was concrete (returned an empty list).

findings.title: PriorityLevel(new_status) may raise ValueError if enum values don't align
findings.body: On line 300, `PriorityLevel(new_status)` converts a `DetectorPriorityLevel` to a `PriorityLevel` by numeric value. If any `DetectorPriorityLevel` member (other than OK, which is handled by the branch above) has a numeric value that does not correspond to a `PriorityLevel` member, this will raise a `ValueError` at runtime. This conversion should be validated or an explicit mapping should be used to ensure safe conversion between the two enum types.

findings.title: Docstring still says 'returns a list' after changing to dict
findings.body: The docstring for `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` (line 230-232) reads 'Evaluates a given data packet and returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`' but the method now returns `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`. This is misleading for future readers.

findings.title: Test uses wrong value for group_2 occurrence construction
findings.body: In `test_state_results_multi_group`, the data packet specifies `{"group_1": 6, "group_2": 10}` (line 177), but the expected occurrence for group_2 is built with value `6` (line 191: `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(detector.detector_handler, "group_2", 6, PriorityLevel.HIGH)`). The actual `build_occurrence_and_event_data` will receive value `10` for group_2. The test passes only because `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` ignores the `value` parameter, meaning the test does not verify that the correct value is passed through to the occurrence builder.
